## Inputs and revision

This teaching model replaces a complete document without overwriting a newer update.
Read retrieves the stored document and its revision, a version number.
Edit prepares a complete replacement using that revision as expectedRevision.
The diagrams follow valid input; schema and policy errors are rejected before this write path and leave storage unchanged.
Let $r$ be the stored revision; an accepted replacement increments it:

$$
r_{next} = r + 1
$$

```typescript
const update = {
  documentId: "4e7efb70-6686-4f94-aa51-f97d40abb677",
  expectedRevision: 3,
  document: completeDocument,
};
```

slides.title: Replacement and retry
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Read["Read"] --> Edit["Edit"]
  Edit --> Write["Write"]
  Write -->|saved| Result["Saved"]
  Write -->|stale| Conflict["No write"]
  Conflict -->|refresh| Read
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Read supplies content and revision; Edit reapplies the intended change and sends a complete replacement to Write.
Write either persists the replacement and returns Saved, or returns a conflict with No write.
The conflict loop returns through both Read and Edit so unrelated updates are retained; it is not a blind retry.

slides.title: Serialized write
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Expected["Expected rev"] --> Compare{"Match?"}
  Current["Stored rev"] --> Compare
  Compare -->|Yes| Commit["Commit"]
  Compare -->|No| Conflict["No write"]

blocks.markdown:
## An uncertain response

A missing write response does not prove that Commit failed.
For this recovery example, assume no competing writer during the check.
Planned update means the complete replacement and its expected next revision.
Read compares both stored content and revision with that plan before another write is attempted.
A changed revision alone does not prove that the planned content was saved.
If another writer can intervene or the result remains ambiguous, stop and investigate.

slides.title: Check before another write
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Read["Read"] -->|stored state| Found{"Saved?"}
  Planned["Planned update"] --> Found
  Found -->|Yes| Stop["No retry"]
  Found -->|No| Edit["Edit"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Saved? compares the stored content and revision from Read with Planned update.
Yes means the planned replacement is present: No retry avoids a second write.
No returns to Edit with the current content and revision rather than resending the old request.
This read-only check does not verify Mermaid, math, readability, or content correctness.

blocks.markdown:
## Conclusion

A replacement succeeds only after validation, a matching revision, and commit.
On conflict, read again and reapply the intended change.
After an interrupted response, inspect stored content and revision before deciding whether to write again.
After saving, open the viewer and check the full article and every slide at desktop and 390px, or report the missing coverage as unverified.
Keep rendering, readability, source correctness, and human acceptance separate from storage success.
